extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys, IP practitioners and businesses seeking patent protection in Malaysia (MyIPO filings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for obtaining, prosecuting, maintaining and enforcing patents (and related instruments like utility innovation certificates) before the Malaysian IP Office (MyIPO), including PCT national phase, examination options, expedited programs, PPH/ASPEC participation, post‑grant matters and infringement/invalidity grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of invention / patentability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is defined as an idea of an inventor which permits in practice the solution to a specific problem in the field of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Malaysia is first-to-file and novelty is generally assessed on an absolute basis (prior art = everything disclosed to the public anywhere in any way before the priority date). Inventive step is assessed based on obviousness to a person having ordinary skill in the art. Industrial application requires the invention can be made or used in any kind of industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty grace period for applicant disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelty grace period of 12 months preceding the Malaysian filing date is available in respect of prior disclosure due to acts committed by, or in abuse of the rights of, the applicant or his predecessor in title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject-matter (express exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions consisting of the following are expressly excluded from patentability: (a) discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; (b) plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals, other than man-made living microorganisms, microbiological processes and products of such processes; (c) schemes, rules or methods for doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games; and (d) methods for the treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy, and diagnostic methods practiced on the human or animal body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion (d) is without prejudice to patentability of a novel medical use of any known substance or composition; in practice first and second medical use claims are normally accepted during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum filing requirements — direct national application
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum requirements for securing a filing date (and priority date): (a) the name and address of the applicant; (b) the name and address of the inventor; (c) a specification comprising a description, claims and any necessary drawings; and (d) the country and filing date of any earlier application whose priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferable (but not essential) to file: priority serial number and IPC symbol (file within 3 months), state of incorporation/nationality of applicant, an abstract, an Appointment of Agent form, and if applicant is not inventor a statement explaining derivation of rights (assignment/employment). These additional items (f–i) may be filed later during preliminary examination. No requirement to file assignment from inventor to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official languages and practice for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The official languages for a Malaysian patent application are English and Bahasa Malaysia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice nearly all applications are filed in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry requirements (Malaysia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for entering Malaysian national phase of a PCT application is 30 months from earliest priority date. Official language is English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum requirements include bibliographic details, one copy of the PCT specification (in or translated to English), copies of any international-phase amendments (in or translated), Form PCT/RO/101 (Request), Form PCT/IB/306 (recording of change), and Form PCT/IB/308 (Second Notice) where applicable. If an English-language specification meeting local formality requirements is publicly available from WIPO, it need not be submitted to MyIPO. Preferable (but not essential) to file Appointment of Agent and derivation statement; these can be filed during preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement into PCT national phase (late national phase entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant that unintentionally fails to meet national phase entry requirements within the 30‑month term may apply for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must pay a surcharge for each month of lateness and submit (i) a written statement of reasons and (ii) a declaration or other evidence in support of the request (MyIPO requires a Statutory Declaration). Maximum term for seeking reinstatement is two months from removal of cause or 12 months from the 30‑month deadline, whichever expires first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document filing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless requested by an examiner, there is no requirement to file a certified copy of any priority application or a translation thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and provisional protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Malaysian patent applications are made available for public inspection after 18 months from the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making available for public inspection confers provisional protection under which, upon grant, the patentee may claim compensation for unauthorized use of the invention prior to grant. International publication of a PCT application designating Malaysia has equivalent effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees on pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no maintenance fees payable on pending Malaysian patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for substantive examination must be filed within: (i) eighteen months of the Malaysian filing date for a direct national application; and (ii) within four years of the international filing date for a PCT national phase application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination options: normal substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal substantive examination: MyIPO will conduct its own search and substantive examination, assisted by results of any search and examination of the same invention in recognized foreign jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for normal examination should be accompanied by (i) filing details of related patent applications in Australia, UK, EPO, Japan, Korea, US and under the PCT; (ii) serial numbers of any patents granted on those applications; and (iii) any available search and examination results including PCT reports. Certified English translations required for documents not in English. A deliberate failure to comply may render the patent liable to invalidation. Examiner may call for further documents during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination options: modified substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified substantive examination may be filed only when a corresponding Australian, European, UK, Japanese, Korean or US patent has been granted for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be accompanied by a certified copy of the foreign patent (and certified English translation if not in English). The Malaysian description, claims and drawings must be brought into substantial agreement with those of the granted foreign patent. Modified examination is a simplified process: checks for novelty, statutory subject matter and compliance with the foreign patent and formal requirements; there is no examination for inventive step and unity of invention. Modiﬁed examination can only be based on a single foreign patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a request for normal or modified substantive examination may be deferred on grounds such as supporting information/documents not yet available or foreign patent not yet granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferment must be applied for within the regular term for requesting examination. Effective 16 August 2006, maximum period of deferment is five years from the Malaysian filing date or international filing date. If unable to file modified examination within deferment, permitted to file a late request for normal examination within three months from expiry of the modified examination deferment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution procedure and response time
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are examined generally in filing date order; filing a request for examination early will not necessarily result in earlier examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term for response to an examination report is two months (three months for applications whose examination request was filed before 15 February 2011). If no timely response or response is unsatisfactory, application may be refused. Applicant may request a hearing if examiner recommends refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary amendment during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: A voluntary amendment of the specification may be filed at any time during the pendency of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter can be added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism / biological deposit practice (no Budapest Treaty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Malaysia has yet to accede to the Budapest Treaty, so no recognition of IDA deposits under Budapest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To fulfill disclosure, applicant must execute a Statutory Declaration confirming they will provide any person requesting a sample of the microorganism/biological material with a declaration addressed to the depositing authority authorizing provision of a sample. The Statutory Declaration is not a filing requirement; it can be submitted during prosecution voluntarily or upon examiner request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an objection of lack of unity is raised during prosecution, applicant may file a divisional application within three months from the mailing date of the examination report containing that objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntary divisional application may be filed only up to the end of a term of three months from the mailing date of the first examination report received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time — general practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The 12‑month convention priority period, 30‑month PCT national phase entry term and the term for requesting examination or deferment are generally not extendible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most other time limits can be extended upon payment of prescribed official fees (fixed fee per extension plus variable fee depending on months sought). Under current practice, term for responding to an adverse substantive examination report may be extended only once and for not more than six months beyond the regular response deadline. Grant of any extension is at Registrar’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination — grounds and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal provisions for requesting expedition of examination exist; no time limit for requesting expedition provided the application has been laid open and a request for examination submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification required by Statutory Declaration and a non-refundable official fee payable. Grounds include: (1) national or public interest; (2) evidence of potential infringement or ongoing infringement proceedings; (3) registration is condition to obtaining monetary grants from Government/institutions recognized by Registrar; (4) invention has been commercialized or applicant intends to commercialize within two years; (5) relates to green technologies enhancing environment or energy conservation; (6) other reasonable grounds. Upon approval, applicant must pay a further substantial official fee for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH is available to expedite Malaysian prosecution based on favourable examination results of a corresponding JP, EP, CN or PCT application (reference application) by JPO, EPO or CNIPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: corresponding relationship (priority/common PCT); one or more claims of reference application indicated as allowable by first Patent Office; claims in Malaysian application sufficiently correspond to allowed claims; normal examination has been requested; if examination request filed previously, examination has not yet started. Required documents: relevant office actions or latest office action containing allowable claims or Written Opinion/IPRP, the claims deemed allowable, any non-patent prior art cited, English translations where applicable. Documents accessible via AIPN/DAS/Patentscope need not be submitted (list suffices). Machine translations admissible; MyIPO may request accurate translation if insufficient. If reference application unpublished, documents must be submitted. MyIPO will decide within two weeks; if accepted, allocated to Examiner and any office action issued within three months; applicant must respond within two months. Final decision on grant should be obtainable within six months of submitting PPH request.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC (ASEAN Patent Examination Cooperation) processing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC allows participating offices to consider search and examination reports of a corresponding application from another participating office to advance prosecution out of turn until grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: corresponding applications (priority/common PCT); a copy of the search report and examination report from the other office plus the claims covered; at least one claim determined allowable; documents filed in English or with verified English translations. No official fee payable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant procedure and immediate post-allowance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon successful completion of substantive examination a clear examination report will be issued and the application will normally proceed to grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application proceeds directly to allowance without issuance of any examination report (effective 01 June 2016): applicant allowed two months for any voluntary amendment and three months for any voluntary divisional application; these terms run from mailing date of the clear report, are not extendible, and grant will be held in abeyance pending expiry unless applicant instructs MyIPO to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of patent and renewal practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent duration depends on filing date: for filing date prior to 01 Aug 2001 the duration is 15 years from grant or 20 years from filing whichever expires later; for filing date on/after 01 Aug 2001 duration is 20 years from filing date (or international filing date for PCT national phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual renewal fee must be paid to keep patent in force; base date for renewal deadlines is date of grant. No back renewal fees payable on grant. First renewal due one year from grant. Each renewal may be paid up to six months late subject to a surcharge of 100% of the regular official fee. Currently no provisions for patent term extension. Appointment of Agent form required when renewal fee first paid by a new agent; official fee payable upon filing Appointment of Agent form since 15 Feb 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of lapsed patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent lapses unintentionally, owner may apply for reinstatement within two years of publication of notice of lapsing in the Government Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition is that non-payment of annual fee was due to accident, mistake or other unforeseeable circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility innovation certificate requirements and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility innovation defined as any innovation creating a new product or process or improvement capable of industrial application; there is no requirement for an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing requirements and prosecution procedure similar to patents. Utility innovation may have only one claim and maximum term is 20 years from filing. Renewal beyond 10 and 15 years from filing is dependent on completing an extension procedure with evidence of commercial or industrial use in Malaysia or a satisfactory explanation of non-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant amendment constraints and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant amendments permissible for correcting clerical errors, obvious mistakes, or any other reason acceptable to the Registrar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance at Registrar’s discretion. Patent must not be subject to Court proceedings at time of amendment. Amendment may not broaden scope of protection conferred at grant nor go beyond disclosure of original specification. Upon filing, amendment forwarded to senior examiner for consideration; no substantive re-examination but examiner may raise objections and applicant given opportunity to respond. If approved, amendment made available for public inspection and notice inserted into Patent Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and acts constituting infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive rights of the patent owner include exploiting the invention, assigning/transmitting the patent, and concluding licence contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement occurs when unauthorized exploitation takes place. No contributory (indirect) infringement in Malaysian patent law. Time limit for infringement proceedings is five years from the acts of infringement (two years for utility innovation certificate). For product patents, infringement comprises making, importing, offering for sale, selling or using the product and stocking such product for sale/use. For process patents, infringement comprises using the process and doing the aforementioned acts in respect of a product obtained directly by the process. Patent right extends only to acts done for industrial or commercial purposes; exclusions include acts solely for uses reasonably related to development and submission of information to regulatory authority (Bolar-type exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidation of a granted patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggrieved person may seek invalidation by application to the High Court on grounds including: (a) the claimed invention is not patentable; (b) the description or claims do not comply with the Patents Regulations; (c) any drawings necessary for understanding were not furnished; (d) the right to the patent does not belong to the person to whom patent was granted; (e) incomplete or incorrect information on corresponding foreign cases has been deliberately provided in connection with a request for normal substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any declaration of invalidity may be partial or full and is effective back to the date of grant (treated as never granted to extent declared invalid).
